text:
maria: Ran a quick perf + flamegraph on Dedicated workload (small-batch bursts) this morning. Seeing a surprising amount of off-CPU time and many context switches during request preprocessing. Attached short notes.

kevin: Nice — did you do a perf + py-spy run or nsys? any kernel timelines? :eyes:

maria: perf + flamegraph (cpu sampling) + py-spy (call stacks). No full nsys GPU trace this time; wanted to isolate CPU side (tokenization, scheduler, batching).

maria: Quick perf command snippet I used:
```
perf record -F 200 -g -p $(pidof inference-worker) -- sleep 45
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```

anika: Can you paste the top collapsed stacks? even a few hot lines helps. Also were you running KV-cache prefetcher enabled? that can push CPU cost from GPU to CPU if aggressive.

maria: Pasting the top hotspots (collapsed style, trimmed):
```
python::tokenize_chunk; batching::BatchingQueue::pop; pthread_cond_wait; memcpy; PyEval_EvalFrameEx; sqlite3_step (audit logging)
```
Observations: tokenization shows up in interpreter frames, a lot of time in pthread_cond_wait -> suggests threads sleeping/waking (context switch churn). memcpy high because of small repeated copies of token buffers when we prefetch k/v shards.

kevin: Huh. So two things: (1) Python tokenizer holding GIL and being run per-request on main worker thread; (2) scheduler uses a central BatchingQueue with a condition variable that wakes many workers for small batches. Both can cause syscalls/context switches.

anika: Agreed. Also noticed py-spy showed ~28-35% in tokenize.py:tokenize_chunk and ~15% in batching code. Off-CPU stacks correlate with pthread_cond_wait while the scheduler waits for batch-fill timeout.

maria: I instrumented with perf record --trace-cmd to get wakeup sources: most wakes originate from enqueue path when tiny bursts arrive (bursty qps). Our current batching heuristic (max_wait_ms=5ms, min_batch=4) results in lots of wakeups for batches of size 1-3.

maria: Small code excerpt from our trace showing the enqueue/wakeup pattern:
```
# simplified
void push_request(req) {
  lock(m);
  queue.push(req);
  if (queue.size() >= min_batch) pthread_cond_signal(&cv);
  unlock(m);
}
```
We signal on every push when near threshold — but bursty clients hit the hot path causing thundering-wake behavior.

kevin: Two low-risk mitigation ideas: 1) exponential backoff aggregation on enqueue (hold wake for a tiny jitter if queue small), 2) move tokenization off the main thread into a pre-tokenize worker pool or native extension to reduce GIL time.

anika: Also consider batching by estimated token length rather than request count for better utilization. And tune prefetched KV shard size — our traces show repeated small memcpy into the KV prefetch buffer. Maybe prefetch fewer shards per-request or aggregate prefetch.

maria: Did a microbenchmark: moving tokenize_chunk into a C extension (pybind11) reduced Python wall time for tokenization by ~2.4x and dropped syscalls by ~40% in a 30s sample. End-to-end p50 latency improved ~12% under synthetic bursty traffic.

kevin: :thumbsup: Can you push that microbench to a branch? we should also add a perf regression test in the perf harness that checks p50 and syscalls for a 1-minute burst scenario.

maria: Branch created: github.com/redwood/inference/compare/tokenize-c-ext. Perf harness change proposed: run 60s burst, record perf counters (context-switches, syscalls) + flamegraph snapshot.

perf-bot: Perf benchmark job #482 finished. flame.svg uploaded to CI artifact (link: https://ci.redwood/perf/482/flame.svg) :robot_face:

anika: For scheduler patch I prototyped a jittered-wakeup: only signal if queue grows by >=2 or if elapsed_since_first >= jitter_ms. Locally reduces wakeups by ~55% and reduces pthread_cond_wait off-CPU time. Patch:
```
if (queue.size() >= min_batch || (queue.size() > 0 && now - first_ts > jitter_ms && queue.size() >= 2)) pthread_cond_signal(&cv);
```

kevin: Nice. Couple of follow-ups: - add metrics (wakeups/sec, avg batch size) to Console so we can correlate with perf runs - run experiment behind feature flag on Dedicated infra - measure KV-prefetch bytes/sec and memcpy hotspot after patches

maria: Agreed. Next steps I will: 1) open PR for tokenizer C extension + perf microbench results 2) open scheduler jitter PR with perf screenshots 3) add wakeup and prefetch metrics to console (small telemetry) 4) run perf regression in CI and post the artifacts.

kevin: Sounds good. Thanks for the investigation and the concise perf artifacts. Once PRs land we can run a full nsys GPU+CPU trace to validate no regression on kernel selection. :eyes:

maria: Thanks — I'll drop the CI links here when results finish. :thumbsup:
